To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the error-prone DNA polymerase ζ/Rev1 complex mediates replication of non-B DNA sequences that are prone to replication stalling.

the error-prone DNA polymerase ζ and Rev1 are recruited to replication forks encountering short hairpin-forming sequences and that Rev1 and Pol ε are responsible for bypassing the hairpin and for the generation of complex mutations that are a signature of Pol ζ.

Pol ζ/ Rev1-dependent mutations occur when replication is stalled at non-B DNA structures and that these mutations arise through template-switching DNA replication and subsequent extension of the misaligned primer terminus by Pol ζ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of replication, repair and recombination of DNA.
understanding the mechanisms of mutagenesis and the role of mutagenesis in the development of cancers.
the molecular mechanisms of DNA replication and repair, and in particular the role of error-prone translesion DNA polymerases in the maintenance of genomic stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNA polymerase ζ and Rev1 play important roles in error-prone bypass and mutagenesis of DNA replication stalling at hairpins and other noncanonical DNA structures.
the Pol ζ/rev1-dependent mutagenic pathway is responsible for the majority of mutations in the absence of damage and is also a major contributor to spontaneous mutagenesis.
DNA Pol ζ and Rev1 are the main players in error-prone bypass and that their activity is stimulated in response to replication disturbances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pol ζ/rev1-dependent mutations are caused by replication stalling at hairpins and that the resulting complex mutations are a result of template-switching DNA polymerase activity.
the Pol ζ/ Rev1 pathway is responsible for the generation of complex mutations at sites of replication stress.
we have discovered a new mutagenic mechanism that is mediated by error-prone translesion polymerases, which is distinct from the previously described mutagenic pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the error-prone bypass mechanism of Pol ζ/Rev 1 can be triggered by replication of undamaged but structurally complex DNA, which can lead to complex mutations that represent an important source of genomic diversity.
the error-prone polymerase Pol ζ is not a backup translesion polymerase that is called into action only after the replicative polymerase has stalled at DNA damage.
Pol ζ and Rev1 are recruited to replication forks that stall at short repeated sequences.
